method: Web search. Several list sites were blocked by the session's network allowlist, so many small countries could not be checked. Status 'supported' means a source named this landmark as the country's best known or most iconic; 'partly' means a source lists it among the country's main sights; 'changed' means the pick was replaced after checking; countries not listed here were not checked.

TG.note: UNESCO describes the Batammariba tower houses (takienta) as a symbol of Togo.

GY.note: Called Guyana's most iconic landmark; featured on banknotes.

SR.note: Major landmark of Paramaribo's UNESCO listed historic inner city; an all wooden cathedral.

MD.note: Reported as the most visited site in Moldova outside the capital; the cave monastery is its centrepiece.

BF.note: The Bobo-Dioulasso mosque is a major mud-brick landmark and is on UNESCO's tentative list. The Ruins of Loropeni is the country's inscribed World Heritage Site.

TO.note: Tonga's best known monument, a coral limestone trilithon at Niutoua on Tongatapu. Location corrected.

SL.note: A confirmed national symbol, on banknotes and stamps. It was felled by a storm on 24 May 2023, so the stamp shows a landmark that no longer stands.

LR.note: No source supported the lighthouse. Sources name the J.J. Roberts Monument, Centennial Pavilion and Providence Island. Switched to the Roberts Monument; no single agreed landmark.

VU.note: Mount Yasur described as the most iconic landmark of Tanna.

AG.note: Devil's Bridge National Park showcases the natural limestone arches.

KN.note: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park is a UNESCO site.

LC.note: The Pitons Management Area near Soufriere.

DM.note: Sources lead with Morne Trois Pitons National Park (UNESCO) and the Boiling Lake. Trafalgar Falls was not named in the results.

BB.note: Main UNESCO site is the Bridgetown Historic Centre and Garrison; the Parliament Buildings sit inside it.

MC.note: Monte Carlo Casino is the most cited attraction.

LI.note: Vaduz Castle is the most frequently named landmark.

SM.note: The Three Towers are the iconic sight.

VA.note: St Peter's Basilica is the main landmark.

LU.note: Sources named Vianden Castle as a picturesque landmark; the Adolphe Bridge was not mentioned. Vianden Castle is the likely alternative.

MT.note: The Azure Window, Malta's best known rock formation, collapsed. Valletta skyline kept as a stand-in.

AD.note: Sources say Andorra's profile rests on skiing rather than a single landmark.

HN.note: Copan Ruins is the top listed landmark in the guide found.

KG.note: Burana Tower, the minaret stump of a destroyed city.

PY.note: One list named Itaipu Dam as Paraguay's landmark. The Jesuit Missions of Trinidad (UNESCO) is kept.

BT.note: Tiger's Nest is described as a national icon of Bhutan. Trongsa Dzong was also named as its most scenic fortress.

KH.note: Angkor Wat appears on the national flag.

NI.note: Results named the Isletas of Granada and Mombacho Volcano; Momotombo was not mentioned.

SV.note: Results named Joya de Ceren and Tazumal; Izalco volcano was not mentioned.

CV.note: Pico do Fogo is widely described as the most iconic landmark of Cabo Verde and the country's highest peak.

CG.note: A travel source calls the Basilique Sainte-Anne one of the most important landmarks of the Republic of the Congo (green tile roof, completed 1943).

ER.note: The Fiat Tagliero Building (1938, aircraft shaped petrol station) is the standout of Asmara, a UNESCO World Heritage city.

LS.note: The mokorotlo (Basotho hat) is on the national flag; the Mokorotlo Building in Maseru is described as Lesotho's most striking architectural landmark.

DZ.note: Maqam Echahid is a 92 m concrete monument (opened 1982) of three palm-leaf shapes over an eternal flame, overlooking Algiers. Confirmed as a major landmark; not shown to be the top national one.

BJ.note: The Door of No Return in Ouidah is a memorial arch to victims of the Atlantic slave trade, about 17 m tall on the seafront.

CF.note: Boali Falls is a well known landmark near Bangui (about 50 m high), shown on a 1963 stamp.

CI.note: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace is described as the world's largest church (dome about 158 m). A major landmark, not described as a national symbol.

KM.note: Mount Karthala is the highest point of the Comoros and an active volcano on Grande Comore.

CD.note: Mount Nyiragongo is an active volcano near Goma whose lava lake draws hikers.

GM.note: Arch 22 in Banjul (built 1996, about 35 m) is a well known landmark. One guide calls it a UNESCO site, which looks like a mix up with Kunta Kinteh Island.

LY.note: The Arch of Septimius Severus is a key landmark of Leptis Magna, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
